title: Magnetoencephalographic Correlates of Clinical Change After Cognitive Processing Therapy in Adults With PTSD
official: REC-Healing Trauma: Clinical and Neurophysiological Mechanisms of Change in Cognitive Processing Therapy for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder. A Single-Arm Proof-of-Concept Pilot Study Using Magnetoencephalography
summary: Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) is a first-line, evidence-based trauma-focused treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), but the clinical and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying therapeutic response remain poorly understood. This single-arm proof-of-concept pilot study will recruit 10 adults with active posttraumatic symptoms who will receive a 12-session 60 minutes individual CPT protocol. Before and after treatment, participants will undergo a clinical assessment and a magnetoencephalography (MEG) recording at the Center for Computational Cognitive Neuroscience (C3N-UCM). The study will test the feasibility of integrating MEG into a therapeutic process and explore whether changes in brain dynamics, particularly connectivity of cognitive-control and autobiographical-memory networks, are associated with clinical improvement.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years.
* Exposure to at least one traumatic event.
* Active posttraumatic symptoms derived from that event (PCL-5 score above cut-off \>= 30).

Exclusion Criteria

* Active suicidal ideation at assessment (PHQ-9 item 9 and clinical judgment).
* Substance dependence.
* Severe cognitive impairment.
* Concurrent trauma-focused individual or group psychotherapy (e.g., Prolonged Exposure, EMDR, CPT).
* Contraindications for MEG: Metallic implants or active devices; claustrophobia.
